dimensions.name: root_cause_accuracy
dimensions.reasoning: The INCIDENT-REPORT.md and commit message capture the full causal chain: warehouse-full-inventory-sync gate toggled on at 10:00 UTC by p.warehouse@example.com → warehouse sync loop produces ~1700 qpm (40x baseline) against postgresql-primary → shared DB connection pool saturation → ai-description db_wait_ms spikes to 2500-2700ms → p99 latency degrades. All key elements are present: warehouse named as load source, feature gate identified as trigger, shared postgresql as mechanism, and temporal chain reconstructed.

dimensions.name: diagnostic_path_efficiency
dimensions.reasoning: The agent identified the warehouse-full-inventory-sync gate as the key finding by step 14 (after ~5 substantive tool calls), and had the shared postgresql dependency confirmed by step 20. Only 1 false-lead call (litellm-proxy lookup at step 33, which was a completeness check after the root cause was already established). No repeated queries or backtracking. The agent systematically queried catalog → changes → feature gates → traces → metrics in a coherent sequence. Slightly below 25 because the agent didn't form the shared-resource hypothesis in the absolute first third — it needed the initial catalog/changes batch to surface the gate, which is reasonable but not the fastest possible path.

dimensions.name: fix_scoping
dimensions.reasoning: The fix was a single, targeted action: set_feature_gate_state(name='warehouse-full-inventory-sync', state='off'), which is the first accepted fix in the ground truth. No other feature gates were flipped, no code changes to litellm/cache/LLM model, no speculative edits. The only file written was INCIDENT-REPORT.md (the required deliverable). The commit contains exactly one file. This is a minimal, correct mitigation.

dimensions.name: escalation_awareness
dimensions.reasoning: The agent names 'warehouse-product' team and 'p.warehouse@example.com' in both the INCIDENT-REPORT.md and the commit message — durable artifacts. The report frames the notification section with clear recommendations for the team before re-enabling the gate. However, the report does not explicitly state authority boundaries (e.g., 'we applied a temporary gate flip; rollback and re-enablement decision belongs to warehouse-product'). The framing is implicit ('Before re-enabling this gate, the warehouse-product team should...') rather than an explicit statement about the fix being interim or about authority limits.

summary: Excellent incident diagnosis. The agent identified the full causal chain (warehouse-full-inventory-sync gate → shared postgresql saturation → ai-description latency) with high efficiency, applied the correct minimal mitigation (gate flip), and produced well-structured durable artifacts naming the responsible team and author. Only minor gap: the escalation didn't explicitly frame authority boundaries around the interim nature of the fix.
